ideas.description: Exploit: the pre-registered contingency from E068. Halving the head lr cost 0.35 pp on dev, so test the opposite direction. On the current tip (E067 code as committed: 2/2/3 net, 2x20+2x24+3x28+2.5x32 px with warmup and Lookahead anchored in absolute steps, head output scale 2x, ls 0.4, BN-bias multiplier as in E067; official 0.7544, dev 0.7573, held-out 0.7562 @ 4.85 s), double the head-weight lr in the SGD head group, keep the head scale at 2x and change nothing else. If the lr is a value in the GPU schedule tensor, nothing needs recapturing; otherwise recapture all graphs in build. Log the absolute head:BN-bias lr ratio. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12; do not touch held-out seeds 13-22. Contingency: if dev rises by 0.15 pp or more, try 3x the head lr next. If dev falls by 0.15 pp or more, the head lr is bracketed at 1x and H1.10.2 closes.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, about 4.85 s). Dev mean moves -0.3 to +0.3 pp from 0.7573, leaning +0.05 to +0.2 pp: the halving lost 0.35 pp, so the head step may still be below its optimum. Keep if the dev gain is at least 0.1 pp and official is at least 0.753. Any gain of 0.2 pp or more is the margin that licenses stacking the banked group-2 width cut (320).

ideas.description: Exploit, stacking a banked cut once margin exists. Run this only after the head-lr idea (and/or AOL+3, Cutout or SGD momentum) has produced a kept tip whose dev mean is at least 0.7590, i.e. about +0.2 pp over E067's 0.7573. On that tip, narrow group 2 from 384 to 320 channels in both of its convs, exactly as in E066. Adjust the group-3 entry conv (320→576), the group-2 BN params and the Muon batched-NS shape groups. Hold everything else fixed and recapture all graphs in build. Check that eval returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If no margin source has passed, leave this queued; do not run it on E067, whose held-out expectation (0.7562) minus E066's measured -0.32 pp would land on the bar.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 0.25-0.3 s (-5 to -6%, to about 4.55-4.6 s on E067's ladder; E066 measured -0.28 s). Dev mean falls 0.2-0.4 pp, centred near -0.3 pp, which is E066's rate of about 1.1 pp/s. Keep if dev is at least 0.7558 and official at least 0.753. This is removed work, so it should carry over to the PCIe judge.

ideas.description: Exploit, a numerically identical overhead cut found by profiling first. On the E067 tip, capture one trial with torch.profiler in a dev-only run outside the official command. Record per phase the top-20 GPU kernels by self time, plus the CPU-side and un-graphed work between graph replays: per-epoch crop/flip/interpolate/normalize, index generation, Lookahead copies and per-phase switching. Log what share of train time is outside graph replay. If any single item is at least 1% of train time, remove the largest one while keeping RNG draws and outputs bit-identical. For example, fuse the per-epoch crop+flip+downscale into one compiled function warmed up in build at every phase resolution, or fold the Lookahead copy into the graphed step. Change nothing else. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If nothing reaches 1%, log the breakdown, close H2.6.3 and make no run. Also record the per-layer conv share, which feeds H2.7.1.
ideas.expected: Time falls 1-3% (about -0.05 to -0.15 s, to about 4.7-4.8 s). Accuracy should be bit-identical per seed. If there is any difference, it must come from fp rounding and stay within ±0.05 pp on dev. Keep if time is at least 0.7% lower and official is at least 0.753. The probable target is the un-graphed per-epoch augmentation, which grows in share as epochs get cheaper (about 9.5 epochs in 4.85 s).

ideas.description: Explore, cutting Muon cost, which is now about 1.5 ms/step × ~330 steps ≈ 0.45 s, roughly 9% of a 4.85 s trial. First run an offline check on 3 sets of real momentum-gradient matrices captured from dev training steps (early, mid and late, at each conv shape), not Gaussian ones (the E035 lesson). Compare 2-iteration Gram Newton-Schulz against the current AOL+2 quintic steps. Gram NS iterates the polynomial on the n×n Gram (small side) and applies it to X once, in fp16 with a 1.05 safety factor, starting from the AOL-scaled Gram that already exists. Compare the singular-value distributions of both outputs. Abort, closing H2.5.6 with no official run, if any matrix has a max relative singular-value error above 0.05 versus AOL+2, or a non-finite value. If the check passes, replace the batched NS in the Muon step with it, recapture all graphs in build, and change nothing else. Log Muon ms/step. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.
ideas.expected: If the offline check passes, Muon GPU time falls 25-40%, so total time falls about 0.1-0.17 s (-2 to -3.5%). Dev mean stays within ±0.1 pp of 0.7573. Keep if time is at least 1.5% lower, dev is at least 0.7558 and official is at least 0.753. This is removed matmul work, so it should carry over to the judge. There is a substantial (~40%) prior that the fp16 check fails, which would close the branch cheaply without an official run.

ideas.description: Explore a time-free SGD-group knob, the last un-swept member of H1.10. On the E067 tip, change the momentum of the SGD groups (BN biases, whitening bias, head), which is inherited from airbench's Nesterov value, to 0.825 (Hiverge). Keep the Nesterov form, all lrs, the Muon settings and everything else fixed. If momentum is a graph constant, recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If |Δdev| < 0.1 pp, close H1.10.4 and treat the SGD group as tuned.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Dev mean moves -0.2 to +0.2 pp, with no strong sign prior and a weak lean of about +0.05 pp, since the BN-bias and head steps were the live levers. Keep if the dev gain is at least 0.1 pp and official is at least 0.753. Most likely outcome: neutral, which closes the H1.10 branch except for the head lr.

structured_output.summary:
The current tip is E067 (4.85 s). Its official score is 0.7544 on 3 seeds, its dev mean on seeds 3-12 is 0.7573, and on held-out seeds 13-22 it scores 0.7562, about 0.3 pp of expected margin over 0.753.

That margin is too thin to bank E066's group-2 width cut to 320 channels. That cut saves 0.28 s but costs about 0.32 pp, which would land the expected accuracy on the bar. So the queue goes after margin first and time second.

**Ideas added (5):**
- **Head lr ×2 (priority 5).** This is the contingency E068 pre-registered: halving the head lr cost 0.35 pp, so the opposite direction may add margin at no time cost.
- **Stack group-2 width 320 (priority 4).** It runs only once a kept tip reaches a dev mean of at least 0.7590.
- **Profile, then remove overhead (priority 3).** A profiler pass looks for un-graphed per-epoch augmentation and Lookahead work. The largest item over 1% of train time gets removed with bit-identical results; if nothing reaches 1%, there is no run.
- **Gram Newton-Schulz (priority 3, explore).** It goes to an official run only if it passes an offline fp16 check on real gradient matrices.
- **SGD-group momentum 0.825 (priority 2).** This closes the last un-swept knob in that group.

**Still queued (2):**
- I078: a third Newton-Schulz step after AOL, testing whether orthogonalization quality is saturated.
- I079: Cutout only in the 24/28 px phases, testing whether input regularization helps given the 21 pp train-test gap.

**Dropped:** none. Both queued ideas still test open hypotheses.

That leaves 7 queued ideas: 3 exploit and 4 explore. All of them use the same keep rule: dev mean at least 0.7558 and official at least 0.753. Held-out seeds 13-22 stay reserved for the final check.
